title: GSTAT Dismisses Appeal for Non-Prosecution After Appellant Skips Three Hearings, Invokes Rule 42
case_name: Shakti Industrial House (Appeal against Order-in-Appeal dated 31 January 2024)
card_summary: The GST Appellate Tribunal dismissed Shakti Industrial House's appeal over a late fee and input tax credit dispute for non-prosecution. The registry had flagged four filing defects, including a missing notice upload and illegible order copies, and the appellant skipped three hearings without explanation. The Tribunal invoked Rules 10 and 42 of the GSTAT Procedure Rules, 2025, leaving the door open for restoration.
card_tip: An unexplained registry defect notice will not fix itself, and three missed hearings can cost an appeal outright; chase every GSTAT defect notice promptly.
verification_notes: Confirmed across TaxGuru, Taxscan/GSTLaw Report and TaxHeal; all three agree on the four filing defects, the three missed hearing dates (15 July, 29 July, 2 September 2026) and the Rule 42 dismissal for non-prosecution without a decision on merits. Decision date taken as 2 September 2026, the date of the final missed hearing; reports were published around 11 September 2026.
